name: Zabad
overview: Zabad is a male figure mentioned in the book of Ezra as a descendant of Nebo. He is notably identified for having married a foreign wife, which was a significant issue addressed during the post-exilic period. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Zabad means 'he bestows' and is a proper name recorded in Ezra 10:43. This name does not appear to have been given by God but reflects a common Hebrew naming convention.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Zabad as a descendant of Nebo, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, no other family relationships are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Zabad's significance lies in his example as one who married a foreign wife during the time of Ezra's reforms, highlighting the challenges faced by Israel in maintaining covenantal purity after the exile. His lineage from Nebo places him within the community affected by these reforms, illustrating the practical implications of the call to holiness and obedience in the restored Israel.
